finding: The complete directed reaction+pathway network (Reactome via Pathway Commons, 119,233 directed product-flow edges incl. 52,989 catalysis-precedes) does NOT out-predict the abstract graph for knockout effects. ESSENTIALITY: reaction-chain out-degree spearman ~0 (-0.05 within-network) vs abstract union degree +0.31; product-cascade reach +0.12 vs degree +0.27. TRANSCRIPTION: no significant advantage over size-matched PPI (p=0.50, n=11). Reason: reaction topology WITHOUT a bypass/mass-balance model over-counts impact -- a protein feeding many downstream reactions is not essential if the products have alternative routes. Bypass modeling is only exactly tractable where mass-balance holds = metabolism, where it IS built and validated (FBA/ecFlux). The reaction chain is a real traceable asset; it just does not beat abstract connectivity for knockout prediction.
